name: E774
full_name: Fermilab E774 Electron Beam Dump Particle Search
summary: E774 operated at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. Its original fixed-target light-particle search must be distinguished from later dark-sector applications.
detection_principle: A high-energy electron beam strikes a dense absorber; a downstream magnetic spectrometer searches for e⁺e⁻ from new-particle decays, with synchrotron radiation aiding electron identification.

key_parameters.name: Original motivation
key_parameters.value: Short-lived particles related to light-e⁺e⁻ resonance anomalies; not originally designed specifically for cosmic dark matter

results.summary: No events consistent with the hypothesized light particle; lifetime-dependent limits were obtained, with additional model dependence in modern dark-photon reinterpretations.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.
